title: What is NELFUND?
content: NELFUND (Nigerian Education Loan Fund) is the Federal Government of Nigeria's interest-free student loan scheme for eligible tertiary students. It can cover institutional charges and/or a monthly upkeep allowance. It is a loan, not a scholarship.

title: What is the purpose of NELFUND?
content: NELFUND exists to make tertiary education more accessible by giving eligible Nigerian students interest-free loans for school charges and, where applicable, upkeep. The purpose is to reduce financial barriers so students are less likely to abandon studies because of fees.

title: Who built or established NELFUND?
content: NELFUND was established by the Federal Government of Nigeria under the Student Loans (Access to Higher Education) Act, 2023. It is a public education-loan fund, not a private app or company product. The Nigerian Education Loan Fund implements the scheme. Always verify current rules on nelf.gov.ng and portal.nelf.gov.ng.

title: Is NELFUND a scholarship?
content: No. NELFUND is a loan. It must be repaid according to NELFUND repayment terms, unlike a scholarship or grant.

title: How do I apply?
content: Apply only through the official NELFUND portal at https://portal.nelf.gov.ng/ — create or verify your account, complete identity/JAMB/institution checks, select components, review, and submit.

title: Where do I log in?
content: Use only https://portal.nelf.gov.ng/ for login and applications. Do not use third-party links from social media.

title: What documents do I need?
content: Commonly needed: NIN, JAMB registration number, admission details, matriculation/student number, personal bank account, and BVN, with consistent name matching. Confirm the exact checklist on the official portal.

title: Who can apply?
content: Eligibility follows official NELFUND rules for the open cycle. Confirm on nelf.gov.ng and portal.nelf.gov.ng — this guide does not invent individual eligibility decisions.

title: What can disqualify an applicant?
content: Disqualification depends on official rules and verification outcomes. Check portal status and official announcements, not social media lists.

title: How much is upkeep?
content: The currently confirmed upkeep amount referenced in this guide is ₦20,000 per month. Treat other figures as unconfirmed unless an official NELFUND source updates them.

title: Does NELFUND pay school fees?
content: NELFUND can cover institutional charges. Where approved, that component is paid to the institution, not as cash to the student. Upkeep is separate when awarded.

title: When do I repay?
content: Repayment terms are set by NELFUND. Current general guidance is that repayment starts after the applicable grace period (often linked to NYSC completion for participants). Confirm your personal schedule on official channels.

title: What is GSI?
content: GSI (Global Standing Instruction) is a repayment recovery mechanism that can be linked to bank accounts. Confirm exact mechanics in official NELFUND documentation.

title: My application is still pending
content: Pending usually means verification steps are still running (identity, JAMB, institution, or bank). Processing time varies. Keep checking the portal and contact your school if institutional verification is stuck.

title: My application was rejected
content: If rejected, read the portal reason carefully, correct any data issues, and follow official reapplication rules for the open cycle. Do not pay agents who claim they can reverse a decision.

title: Portal shows missing school information
content: Missing school information often means your institution has not uploaded or matched your student record yet. Contact the office that handles NELFUND at your school and keep checking the portal.

title: Has my school uploaded my data?
content: Institution upload status is controlled by your school. If your record is missing, ask the NELFUND coordination / ICT / registry team at your institution to confirm submission to NELFUND.

title: I already paid school fees
content: If you paid fees before NELFUND disbursement, ask your institution about their refund or reconciliation process. Institutional charges are paid to the school, so refund policy is usually institution-side.

title: How do I contact NELFUND?
content: Use official channels listed on nelf.gov.ng and the portal. Prefer written records. For school-record issues, contact your institution NELFUND office as well.

title: Is someone asking me to pay to process NELFUND?
content: Do not pay agents who claim they can process, speed up, or guarantee NELFUND approval. Apply only through portal.nelf.gov.ng and never share OTPs or bank passwords.

title: Do I need a guarantor?
content: Guarantor requirements depend on current official application rules. Confirm on the portal for your cycle rather than relying on older social media posts.
